titles.title: Datasets and Python Notebooks for: Marine Cloud Brightening and Precipitation Responses in the Tropical Pacific Ocean

descriptions.description:
This repository contains datasets and Jupyter notebooks used for the analyses presented in the manuscript:

"Marine Cloud Brightening and Precipitation Responses in the Tropical Pacific Ocean"

submitted to AGU Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres in June 2026.

Preprint: https://essopenarchive.org/doi/full/10.22541/essoar.15005398/v1Note: The manuscript is subject to change after revision.

Contents include:- Processed datasets used in the study- Python notebooks for (preprocessing) bias-correction workflows- Python notebooks for data analysis and figure generationSome preprocessing notebooks rely on external datasets associated with previously published work:

Hirasawa, H., M. Henry, A. M. Mason, P. J. Rasch, S. J. Doherty, R. Wood, J. Haywood, & K. Von Salzen (2026a). Forcing susceptibility and climate sensitivity to midlatitude Marine Cloud Brightening. Journal of Climate, 39, 769-784. https://doi.org/10.1175/JCLI-D-25-0337.1

These external datasets, i.e., Earth system model outputs for CESM2, E3SMv2, and UKESM1, are not redistributed in this repository and are available from the original authors upon reasonable request.

repository/├── data_NarenpitakEtAl2026_forRepository.tar.gz│ ├── era5│ ├── MCB_patch/cesm2/biascorrection│ ├── MCB_patch/e3smv2/biascorrection│ ├── MCB_patch/ukesm1/biascorrection│ └── World_Countries_Shapefiles├── analysis_notebooks/│ ├── NarenpitakEtAl2026 - Fig1_dTmap_region - Fig11_dT_dP_NH-SH_region - Fig12 - FigS20-21.ipynb│ ├── NarenpitakEtAl2026 - Fig2-5_Zonal_Means.ipynb│ ├── NarenpitakEtAl2026 - Fig6-8_Meridional_Means.ipynb│ ├── NarenpitakEtAl2026 - Fig9_Composites_dT_dP - SI_FigS5-S18.ipynb│ └── NarenpitakEtAl2026 - Fig10_ScatterPlot_IndexVsP.ipynb├── preprocessing_notebooks/│ ├── biascorrection_MCBruns_T_1_compute_dT.ipynb│ └── biascorrection_MCBruns_T_2_compute_new_T.ipynb│ ├── biascorrection_MCBruns_P_1_compute_dP.ipynb│ └── biascorrection_MCBruns_P_2_compute_new_P.ipynb├── README.md└── NarenpitakEtAl2026_supporting_information.pdf

To run the preprocessing_notebooks, Earth system model outputs for CESM2, E3SMv2, and UKESM1 are required. The original outputs are not redistributed in this repository and are available from the original authors upon reasonable request.

These scripts   ├── biascorrection_MCBruns_T_1_compute_dT.ipynb   ├── biascorrection_MCBruns_P_1_compute_dP.ipynbregrid the original ESM outputs to 0.5 x 0.5 degrees resolution and compute factors for biascorrecting near-surface temperature (T), near-surface specific humidity (Q), and precipitation (P) for CESM2, E3SMv2, and UKESM1, between 40 degrees S and 40 degrees N.

The files can be found in

data_NarenpitakEtAl2026_forRepository/├──  MCB_patch/├──├── cesm2/├──├──├── biascorrection/dP_era5_cesm_CTL_2015-2024_P_0.5deg.nc├──├──├── biascorrection/dQ_era5_cesm_CTL_2015-2024_Q_0.5deg.nc├──├──├── biascorrection/dT_era5_cesm_CTL_2015-2024_T_0.5deg.nc├──├── e3smv2/└──└── ukesm1/

These scripts   └── biascorrection_MCBruns_T_2_compute_new_T.ipynb   └── biascorrection_MCBruns_P_2_compute_new_P.ipynbuse the original ESM outputs and the biascorrecting factors, and produce the biascorrected ESM outputs.

The biascorrected ESM outputs (bc_*nc) and can be found in the following directory:

data_NarenpitakEtAl2026_forRepository/├──  MCB_patch/cesm2/biascorrection/├──  MCB_patch/e3smv2/biascorrection/├──  MCB_patch/UKESM1/biascorrection/

and are used in the analysis in the analysis_notebooks.

This research was funded by the Degrees Initiative through the Degrees Modelling Fund (DMF) and the DMF Continuation Grant (Grant Number: RGA-DMF-THA-01-25-C1).

titles.title: Ancient Civilizations, Endogenous Catastrophes, Glaciations and the HFTPW Model

rightsList.rights: Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial 4.0 International

descriptions.description: A geodynamic model is proposed for the repositioning of the Earth’s rotational axis (High-Frequency True Polar Wander, HFTPW), induced by the asymmetric redistribution of masses within the mantle. The planetary model proposed here is a hollow-shell model (HES) [1], comprising a crust, a mantle and a core with an inverse density gradient, an inner crust, and a primordial black hole (PBH) at its center. The planetary magnetic field is hypothesized to be generated by a toroidal accretion disk (TAD) orbiting the PBH. The present study postulates recurrent catastrophes arising from causes endogenous to the planet. The most recent of these events, dated to approximately 424,000 years ago, is correlated with a displacement of the geographic poles across the Earth’s surface, namely a rotation of the shell relative to the axis, which remains fixed with respect to the stars. Subsequent re-diffusion or renewed displacement of the anomalous mass within the mantle triggered a variable-speed repositioning of the rotational axis along a preferred meridian, identifying six quasi-stable stages alternating with transitional periods of polar migration. The six quasi-stable stages were established through the statistical analysis of the orientations of ancient megalithic complexes conducted by M. Buildreps [2], and are consistent with paleoclimatic data, including the anomalies of the MIS 11 event. The model also accounts for the most recent glacial periods. The temperature decline during periods of axial transition is a direct consequence of the rapid melting of polar ice displaced into warm latitudes, which destroys ocean circulation (AMOC), while winds generated by Coriolis realignment and the mixing of abyssal waters cool the atmosphere. Periods of axial quasi-stability allow the crust and oceans to attain hydrostatic and thermal equilibrium; ocean circulation transports heat efficiently, and the Earth’s temperature rises toward an interglacial optimum. Within this model, therefore, the catastrophes and floods described in ancient traditions are not merely myths, but memories of real events caused by the planet’s impulsive endogenous dynamics.
